description: Unlike most recordings in this archive, which were captured from the audience on a small microphone, this one was recorded directly from the soundboard to DAT — so the sound is unusually clear and close.
The full tape has been split into its 30 individual songs: Jerry’s originals alongside traditional Irish songs and a handful of covers. Each track can be streamed right here.
These tracks have not been normalized yet, so they may sound a little low in volume — that will be fixed later.
A couple of notes on the set: the song listed as “Scallywag” (track 6) is a placeholder — I can no longer recall its real name. The tape also captures early versions of “This World” and “Woman.”

description: Recorded directly from the soundboard to DAT at 19 Broadway in Fairfax, this is one of the clearer recordings in the archive. The full night has been split into its 31 individual songs — Jerry’s originals alongside traditional Irish songs and a handful of covers.
All 31 songs have now been volume-normalized for a consistent, comfortable listening level across the set.

A few of the songs here are obscure, unfinished sketches. “Loser,” “Xmas Song,” and “Blender” are short ideas more than full songs. “Dope World” may never have been finished, and “Slave Woman” was a very early song that — for obvious reasons — was rarely featured in live shows.
On the last song of the night, “The Old Triangle,” a guest singer named Johnny joins Jerry.

description: 19 Broadway is a small, famously loud bar in Fairfax, and this night was no exception — the room was packed and talking straight through the set. The tape was captured from the audience on a DAT recorder, so you’ll hear the crowd, the clink of glasses, and the bar’s heavy front door banging open and shut between songs.

Despite the racket, Sean played a long, generous set. The full tape has been split into its 31 individual songs — Sean’s originals alongside traditional tunes and a handful of covers. Each track streams here for free as a 320 kbps MP3, or can be downloaded as a lossless FLAC (password protected).
The songs from this show have not been normalized yet, so they may sound a little low in volume — that will be fixed later.
“Model Family Man” was originally written by the Hannans’ friend Paddy Nash in Ireland.

description: Unlike the audience tapes that make up most of this archive, this February 2000 set at 19 Broadway was recorded straight off the soundboard — so it’s unusually clean and close, with Sean’s voice and guitar right up front.

The tape has been split into its 11 songs — Sean’s originals alongside a few traditional Irish tunes and covers. Each track streams here for free as a 320 kbps MP3, or can be downloaded as a lossless FLAC (password protected).
In all this is a relatively short set for Sean. Both the streaming MP3s and the lossless FLAC files have been normalized in Audacity for a more even listening level.
On “Plastic Lemons” it is actually Jerry Hannan singing — he stepped in for a song while Sean, who was quite tired this night, took a break.
The full tape also includes some guitar music from an unidentified musician, and has not yet been fully audited.
